10.1a — 3-Button Jam: Brainstorm & Pitch

Welcome back from Winter Break! From now through the end of Semester 1 (January 21), you are running your first real game jam. There is only one mechanical constraint: your entire game runs on at most three buttons of input. Today is all about divergent brainstorming, stress-testing ideas against that 3-button rule, and pitching a scope you can actually prototype, playtest, and revise in three weeks.

The Constraint: Three Buttons Total ~10 min

"Three buttons" means three discrete inputs total across the entire active game (for example: A + D + Space; Left Arrow + Right Arrow + Up Arrow; J + K + L; or two keys + left mouse click).

  • No hidden inputs: WASD is already 4 buttons! Aiming with the mouse cursor while pressing keys counts mouse movement + keys — keep it honestly to three physical presses.
  • Why 3 instead of 10? Fewer buttons force every input to pull double duty (tap vs. hold, press both together, context actions, auto-movement with lane switches or gravity flips). That constraint eliminates clutter and lets testers understand your controls in five seconds.
  • Menus stay inside the 3 buttons: Start Game and Retry should use one of your 3 gameplay buttons so a tester never searches the keyboard.
Brainstorm Flood: Five Ideas Before You Pick (~20 min) ~20 min

First ideas are almost always clones of games you already played. Force yourself to sketch five genuinely different 3-button concepts in 15 minutes before falling in love with one:

#Working Idea / GenreButton 1Button 2Button 3Why It Could Break
1e.g. Auto-runner + shield + dashJump / Double JumpDashShield / Parry
2
3
4
5

Ways to get weird with 3 buttons:

  • 2-axis spin + fire: rotate left, rotate right, thrust/shoot forward (classic arcade asteroids).
  • 3-lane rhythm / catcher: top lane, middle lane, bottom lane (pressing a button snaps directly to that track!).
  • Shared-keyboard 1v1 or co-op? Two players with only 3 buttons total (1+1+shared switch, or 3 shared actions!).
  • Hold vs. Tap / Physics Switch: button 1 flips gravity, button 2 swaps color/phase, button 3 brakes or fires.
Filter, Cut Scope & Pitch (~25 min) ~25 min

Pick ONE winner from your five sketches, run the scope check, and pitch it to two classmates before opening Unity:

  1. The Cheat Check: trace ten seconds of gameplay aloud — if you ever say "and then they press W or aim with the mouse," fix the mechanic or pick another idea from your table.
  2. One Loop, One Arena: write down your single win/score condition, single fail condition, and the one thing that escalates difficulty over time (never five separate levels for a two-to-three-week jam).
  3. Name the Riskiest Part First: write down which mechanic in your pitch you have NEVER built before — that is the very first thing you greybox next class.
  4. 2-Minute Desk Pitch: explain your game to two classmates using ONLY: (1) Goal, (2) What Buttons 1, 2, 3 do, and (3) Why it gets tense. Ask them: "Wait — what happens if I press Button 2 twice?" Update your spec on the spot if their question exposes a flaw.

Socratic: Designing Inside a Constraint

What is your committed pitch — Game Title, exact 3 buttons with keys, Win/Score rule, Fail rule — and which of your five brainstormed ideas did you cut and why?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Fill out five distinct 3-button concepts without sneaking in a fourth input
  • Commit to one scoped core loop with clear win, lose, and escalation rules
  • Pitch your 3-button controls cleanly to two classmates and answer their edge-case questions
  • Save your pitch notes cleanly in your project repo (and start a fresh Unity scene/repo as instructed)
